answer: Randomised submission windows: each epoch, slots open at unpredictable times derived from a per-identity cipher, so one operator cannot batch-mine. Temporal diversity forces attackers to run always-on infrastructure across many grove-sharded identities. Sybil farm of 100 identities needs 100x monitoring uptime plus 100x jade deposits locked per slot; a solo honest miner needs one. Rent alone hits $12/slot x 100 = $1,200/day versus linear rewards. Cost scales quadratically while honest yield stays flat, so the mechanism works because batch advantage disappears.
